subtype: Approach: calming with slow breaths before going on [Action]
passage: The curtain was two minutes from opening. Vasudha stood in the wings in her yellow costume, and her heart beat so hard she could feel it in her ears. Charu, next to her, was fidgeting with a bangle. "Do the breathing," whispered Vasudha, remembering what the dance teacher had shown the group. She breathed in through her nose, counting one, two, three, four. Then out through her mouth, one, two, three, four. Again. Again. Her hands stopped shaking. Her heartbeat slowed, and her shoulders dropped. When the music began she stepped forward, not calm exactly, but steady enough to start.

qa.q: What was Vasudha feeling before the curtain opened?
qa.a: Vasudha was nervous, shown by her loud heartbeat and shaking hands, until the slow breaths steadied her.

qa.q: What alternative approach could Vasudha use if breathing is not enough, and why?
qa.a: Vasudha could tell the first step of the dance to herself or hold a friend's hand for a moment. A small thing to focus on gives the mind somewhere to go.

qa.q: How might Charu see Vasudha's breathing?
qa.a: Charu was fidgeting with a bangle and heard the whisper to breathe, so Charu may find it a comfort and may copy it to settle down too.

grounding: Before the dance a girl breathes in slowly for four counts and out for four, as her teacher showed the group, so her heart slows and her hands steady.

subtype: Approach: calming with slow breaths before going on [Action]
passage:
"Sudha, your hands are shaking."
"Vishal sir, I can't. Everyone's out there."
"Remember what we did in class? Show me. Hand on your tummy."
"In, two, three, four."
"Good. Out."
"Out, two, three, four."
"Again."
"In, two, three, four... out, two, three, four."
"How's the heart?"
"Still fast."
"Twice more."
Sudha breathed, eyes on the curtain rope.
"Now?"
"Slower." She held up her hand. "Not shaking."
"That's it. Take your spot."
The music began, and Sudha walked on counting her first eight steps.

qa.q: Where does Vishal sir tell Sudha to put her hand?
How was Sudha feeling before the breathing?
qa.a: She was very nervous, with shaking hands and a racing heart at the thought of the audience.

qa.q: What other approach could help Sudha if breathing is not enough?
qa.a: She could quietly mark her first steps in the wings, because moving her body through the start can calm nerves too.

qa.q: How does the moment look to Vishal sir?
qa.a: Vishal sir sees a scared student and calmly reminds her of the class exercise, then is pleased when her hands steady.

grounding: It shows a girl using slow four-count breathing, taught by her teacher, to calm her heart and steady her hands before a dance.

subtype: Approach: calming with slow breaths before going on [Action]
passage: Before our Bihu dance at the school function, I thought I was going to be sick with nerves. My friend Devika, who dances next to me, grabbed my arm backstage. "Jasleen, the breathing," she whispered. Our dance teacher had taught all of us girls in the group: breathe in for four, out for four, with a hand on your stomach. We did it together, looking at each other. In, two, three, four. Out, two, three, four. The first time, my heart was still racing. The fourth time, I could feel it slow down, and my hands stopped fiddling with my dupatta. When the drum began, I walked out steady. Now I do it before tests as well.

qa.q: What did Jasleen's hands stop fiddling with?
qa.a: Jasleen's hands stopped fiddling with the dupatta.

qa.q: How was Jasleen feeling backstage before the breathing?
qa.a: Jasleen was very nervous, with a racing heart and restless hands.

qa.q: Which other situation could Jasleen use this approach in, and why?
qa.a: Jasleen already uses it before tests; it could also help before speaking in class, since slow breaths work anywhere nerves rise.

qa.q: How might the breathing together feel to Devika?
qa.a: Devika feels useful and calmer too, since doing it together steadies both of them.

grounding: It shows a girl breathing slowly for four counts in and out, as taught by the teacher, to slow her heart and steady her hands before a dance.
